The '''standard model of particle physics''' explains the hundreds of [[quantum particle]]s known to human and their various simple and complex interactions by less than 20 [[fundamental particle]]s.

== Current model ==

[[File:Reality stew.png|thumbnail|A food-loving physicist's impression of the standard model]]

=== Fundamental particles ===

As of 2026, the current standard model of particle physics include 17 [[fundamental particle]]s and their corresponding [[antiparticle]]s confirmed to exist:

* 6 [[lepton]]s and their antileptons,
* 6 [[quark]]s and their antiquarks,
* 5 [[boson]]s.

<blockquote>
All fundamental particles have a corresponding antiparticle. The [[antiparticle]] of a boson is also a boson.
</blockquote>

=== Composition ===

All known [[ordinary matter]] particles are composites of quarks and/or leptons.

All known [[antimatter]] particles are composites of antiquarks and/or antileptons.

[[Meson]]s are half matter and half antimatter.

=== Interaction ===

Matter and antimatter particles interact with each other via [[boson]]s. Interactions between all particles, fundamental or composite, can be described by four [[fundamental interactions]].
